evidence: Draft judged: "Have you got any sense of what it is that's making it feel fake?" Read cold in CONTEXT, it is the first line under the heading "It feels fake". The "it" in "making it feel fake" is the heading's "It" (the practice the reader is trying), and the following fragment ("The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc.") reads naturally as the answer to "what's making it feel fake", so the pronouns land and the order follows from the heading. The draft occurs once in CONTEXT and is word for word the sentence the_change quotes (Emulate, sample co), with no AI fix added, so it does what the_change says. Against SOURCE (replaced: "Do you have a sense of what it is that feels fake?"; guide: "First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you're trying to perform."): the meaning is kept, one question asking the reader to find what about the practice feels fake, with the same candidates in the unchanged list after it. The only shift is "what feels fake" (which part) to "what's making it feel fake" (which part causes it); with that list after it the two read the same, and the draft adds no claim, fact or first-person statement. Voice: "Have you got" is slightly British, but it matches "see how you get on" later in the section and the plain, loosely punctuated register around it (comma-spliced sentences, "etc" with no full stop); the straight apostrophe matches the neighbouring "doesn't" / "don't". Tell rows: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the draft in its context and find none PRESENT. Closest calls, all judged absent: T19/T24 (a question followed straight away by a list of candidate answers) is the guide's own step with the same question-then-list order in his published sentence, the heading is the reader's complaint so the question is a real one, and no suspense is staged; T15 (a rewording) is common words swapped ("Have you got any", "is making it feel") with no rare-synonym substitution over an AI skeleton, and there is no other tell for the structure to carry; T22 (the paragraph around it is coach register, but that is unchanged text, and the draft is a diagnostic question, not reassurance); T26 (it echoes the heading's "feels fake", which anchors "it" and is the section's subject); T07 ("any sense of" is an ordinary question hedge, not a staged filler); C02 pointer is right. Linter: "D9 follows the source order" is accepted: one sentence replacing one sentence makes agreement 1.00 automatic, and the noticing T13/T09 ask for sits in the unchanged text around it (the aside that it doesn't matter not having an inner voice/image, the part that is protecting you), which the change neither adds nor removes. "E36/E41 heavy second person" (7.1 "you" per 100 words) is accepted: it is one "you" in a 14-word direct question to the reader in a guide written in the second person throughout, as the replaced sentence also had, with no second-person scenery. One note outside the verdict: the writer's ADMISSION.json gives T14/T15 evidence about putting back a point Emulate dropped, which does not describe this change (no put-back here); my own reading finds both rows absent, so the verdict is unaffected.
